intro: Turn raw model scores into probabilities. Softmax sits at the heart of classifiers and attention, but a direct implementation can break on large numbers.
task: Implement softmax(x) for a one-dimensional array of finite numbers. Return a NumPy array of probabilities without changing the input.
requirements: Accept a numeric list or a nonempty one-dimensional array.
Return finite, nonnegative probabilities that sum to one.
Raise ValueError for empty, non-finite, or non-1D input.
Leave the original input unchanged. Very small probabilities may underflow to zero.

hints.title: Start with the contract
hints.body: Convert x with np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64). Check dimensions, size, and finiteness before doing any math.

hints.title: Keep exponentials small
hints.body: Subtract the largest score. The largest shifted score is zero, so its exponential is one.

hints.title: Normalize the weights
hints.body: Compute the exponentials, then divide by their sum. At least one weight is one, so the normalizer is positive.

explanation: Subtracting one value from every score multiplies each exponential by the same factor. That factor cancels during normalization, so the probabilities stay the same.

Subtracting the maximum ensures every exponential is at most one. With extreme finite inputs, a negative shifted score can overflow to negative infinity; its exponential is zero, the appropriate limiting probability.
Softmax produces relative probabilities. Adding a constant changes no probabilities, while scaling scores changes how concentrated the distribution becomes.
formula: softmax(x)ᵢ = exp(xᵢ − max(x)) / Σⱼ exp(xⱼ − max(x))
